title: Frame-action descent of compared vector-bundle traces
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient data of [def-pur-conventions], put $A=A_{E,n}$ with $n\geq1$, and let $S$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], without assuming $S$ separated over $k$. For every scheme $T$ used below, work in the ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on its small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], with comparison $C_T=\nu_T^*$ [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback] and derived tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Choose $r\geq1$ with $\ell^rA=0$, write $L_{T,r}=\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{\ell^r,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}A_T$, and use the root-projection comparison $C_TL_{T,r}\cong A_T(1)$ and its tensor powers [lem-amb-finite-tate-site-descent, def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. For a separated finite-type map $f:X\to Y$ with compactification $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,p:\overline X\to Y)$, let $F_f^e=Rp_{e,*}j_!^e$ and $F_f^p=Rp_{p,*}j_!^p$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Use precisely $B_f=Rp_{p,*}(e_j)\circ\beta_{p,j_!}:C_YF_f^e\xrightarrow{\sim}F_f^pC_X$, where $\beta$ is the counit-mate comparison and $e_j$ the adjoint extension comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate, lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison].
Let $\pi:V\to S$ be a vector bundle of constant rank $d\geq0$ [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section], compactified by its projective completion $V\xrightarrow{j}\overline V\xrightarrow{\overline\pi}S$ [lem-amb-vector-projective-completion]. Put $M^e=F_\pi^eL_{V,r}^{\otimes d}[2d]$ and $M^p=F_\pi^pA_V(d)[2d]$. Suppose for every open $W\subseteq S$ there are ordered pro-etale coordinate traces $t_{d,W}^p$ on $\mathbf A^d_W$ which are isomorphisms, commute with open restriction, and satisfy $t_{d,W}^pB_{p_{d,W}}=C_W(t_{d,W}^e)$ for the ordinary traces of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]. Suppose $B$ satisfies the refinement, composition and open-restriction identities of [lem-pur-compact-support-site-coherence]; $B$ is the comparison of [def-sf-compact-support-site-comparison-construction]. On a finite trivializing open cover $\{U_i\}$ let $a_i^e:M^e|_{U_i}\to A_{U_i}[0]$ and $a_i^p:M^p|_{U_i}\to A_{U_i}[0]$ be the actual compact-support restriction exchanges followed by the coordinate identifications and the traces $t_{d,U_i}^e,t_{d,U_i}^p$; $a_i^p$ is the local pro-etale integration on a frame of [def-pur-proetale-frame-integration], built from the ordered integration of [def-pur-proetale-ordered-integration] (these definition nodes index the coefficient ring as $\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{n'+1}$ and the exponent by $\ell^{r'+1}A=0$; take $n'=n-1$, $r'=r-1$).
For every overlap $W=U_i\cap U_j$ and coordinate change $G\in\mathrm{GL}_d(\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W))$, the action of $[x_0:x]\mapsto[x_0:Gx]$ on the projective completion intertwines $B$ with the compact-support frame action. The maps $a_i^p$ agree on overlaps. The derived objects $M^e,M^p,C_SM^e$ are canonically their degree-zero cohomology sheaves placed in degree zero. There is a unique global morphism $t_\pi^p:M^p\to A_S[0]$ restricting to all $a_i^p$ (the map of [def-pur-proetale-vector-integration]), it is an isomorphism, it is independent of the trivializing cover and frames, and
$$t_\pi^pB_\pi=C_S(t_\pi^e),$$
where $t_\pi^e$ is the prescribed ordinary global integration [def-amb-vector-integration]. These assertions use degree-zero derived-map gluing [lem-pur-degree-zero-derived-map-gluing]; no affineness of the overlaps and no descent assertion for arbitrary derived morphisms is assumed. They include rank zero and the empty base with its empty cover.

Naturality of the actual derived pullback comparison and the ordinary all-frame normalization show that vectorSite followed by the compared ordinary integration satisfies VectorNormalization. proof.text: The existing ordinary geometric descent theorem gives concentration of the ordinary vector source in degree zero and invertibility of its prescribed trace. Transport concentration through the canonical compactification change. Exact comparison preserves concentration; the actual site isomorphism transports it to the pro-etale source. The unique H0-normalized single-object isomorphism gives all three degree-zero clauses.

proof.text: The all-frame defining normalization of vectorIntegration, after the canonical source change, is exactly frameDescentLocal. Naturality of the exact/left-derived comparison proves that frameDescentGlobal restricts to each such local morphism. Degree-zero derived-map equality detection gives unique gluing on the displayed cover, and the gluing equivalence implies overlap agreement. The comparison from the first step and canonical source-change cancellations give the final site equation and invertibility. These arguments allow rank zero and an empty cover.

proof.text: For every linear frame automorphism use its already constructed Cartesian affine square. Apply compactSupport_exchange_transport to the bounded Tate input. Naturality of the site comparison in the canonical coefficient isomorphism identifies the target factor. The bounded/unbounded etale exchange compatibility identifies the ordinary factor. Identity coherence of the underived pullback comparison, carried through exact derived functors, cancels the identity base pullback. Postcompose with the same normalized compactification change on both sides; cancellation gives FrameActionIntertwining for the independently defined two actions. No projective extension construction is needed because the transport theorem applies to any chosen compactification of this square. The bounded input is kept folded with its proved defining object equality; the coefficient map is transported only through this equality. Generic ordinary and pro-etale action composites retain the original arrow order and are specialized to this input. These definitional APIs avoid expensive repeated endpoint unfolding.

proof.text: For the finite-type specialization, finite type over the coefficient field gives a Noetherian base. Invertibility of the coefficient prime follows from its existing stalkwise invertibility and the local criterion for units. Apply the two preceding theorems on the base and every open, with the inherited unit condition. This preserves the full projective-completion and every-frame assertions.
